blocks.alt: Input text goes through an encoder stack to produce a rich representation

blocks.text: Attention Masks, the final topic of the previous Transformers module, closed out coverage of every masking technique needed here. Encoder-Only Models open the Transformer Architectures module, using genuinely just the encoder half already covered.
These models use genuinely just the encoder half already covered, dropping the decoder entirely, a genuinely important, focused architectural family covered throughout the rest of this topic.
2. Recapping When The Encoder Alone Suffices

This connects back to recognizing when using just the encoder alone is genuinely sufficient, already covered in The Encoder. Tasks needing genuinely rich understanding but no genuinely sequential output, already covered there.
This topic genuinely explores that exact family of architectures in complete depth, giving that earlier general observation its own genuinely complete, dedicated treatment.
3. Why Drop The Decoder

blocks.alt: Encoder-decoder is compared against encoder-only when no generation is needed

blocks.text: This connects back to the decoder's own output-generating role, already covered in The Decoder. Some tasks genuinely need understanding, not generation, already covered generally throughout this course.

Dropping the decoder entirely genuinely simplifies the architecture for exactly these tasks, avoiding the genuinely unnecessary complexity of a component whose own core purpose these tasks simply do not need.
4. Bidirectional Context

blocks.alt: Left context and right context both feed into bidirectional attention

blocks.text: A genuinely important, distinctive property connects back to encoder Self-Attention needing no causal masking, already covered in Causal Masking. Every position genuinely attends freely to every other position, both before and after it.

This genuinely bidirectional view, already covered in this section, is a genuinely important, distinctive strength of Encoder-Only Models compared with the genuinely restricted, forward-only view already covered for decoders.

blocks.text: 5. A Rich Representation As The Output

blocks.alt: Encoder output produces a dense vector per token

blocks.text: This connects back to what the encoder output genuinely represents, already covered in The Encoder. The genuinely final output represents every input position, enriched with context from the entire sequence.
This is exactly the same rich representation already covered there, now the genuinely final product rather than an intermediate step feeding into a decoder, already covered as that earlier role.
6. Adding A Classification Head

blocks.alt: Encoder output feeds a classification head to produce a label

blocks.text: This connects back to Image Classification's own output layer, already covered in its own topic. A genuinely small classification head often gets added on top of the encoder's own final output.

This produces genuinely task-specific predictions, like sentiment or category labels, directly reusing the same final-layer philosophy already covered throughout Image Classification for a genuinely different data type.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When Encoder-Only Models Are Genuinely The Right Choice

blocks.alt: Needing an understanding task points toward using an encoder-only model

blocks.text: This connects back to Sentiment Analysis, Named Entity Recognition, or genuinely other classification-style tasks. Encoder-Only Models, already covered in this topic, directly suit these genuinely understanding-focused tasks.
Not needing genuinely sequential text generation at all is another genuine case where Encoder-Only Models, already covered, avoid the genuinely unnecessary decoder complexity.
10. Worked Example

The example below directly demonstrates an Encoder-Only Model's own pipeline, from token embedding through encoder layers to a final classification head, illustrating the concepts already covered throughout this topic.

code.content:
import numpy as np

rng = np.random.RandomState(42)
sequence_length = 6
hidden_size = 8
num_classes = 3  # already covered as adding a classification head in this topic

def softmax(x):
    exp_x = np.exp(x - np.max(x, axis=-1, keepdims=True))
    return exp_x / exp_x.sum(axis=-1, keepdims=True)

def encoder_layer(x, rng):
    # already covered as bidirectional context in this topic: no causal masking needed
    W_q, W_k, W_v = [rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1 for _ in range(3)]
    q, k, v = x @ W_q.T, x @ W_k.T, x @ W_v.T
    weights = softmax(q @ k.T / np.sqrt(hidden_size))  # no mask applied at all
    x = x + weights @ v
    x = x + np.tanh(x @ (rng.normal(size=(hidden_size, hidden_size)) * 0.1))
    return x

hidden_representation = rng.normal(size=(sequence_length, hidden_size))
for _ in range(2):
    hidden_representation = encoder_layer(hidden_representation, rng)

# already covered as a rich representation as the output in this topic
pooled_representation = hidden_representation.mean(axis=0)  # a genuinely simple pooling strategy

# already covered as adding a classification head in this topic
W_classifier = rng.normal(size=(num_classes, hidden_size)) * 0.1
class_probabilities = softmax(W_classifier @ pooled_representation)

print(f"Pooled representation shape: {pooled_representation.shape}")
print(f"Class probabilities: {np.round(class_probabilities, 3)}")
print(f"Predicted class: {np.argmax(class_probabilities)}, already covered as adding a classification head in this topic")

blocks.text: 11. Key Takeaways

items: Encoder-Only Models use just the encoder half of the Transformer, dropping the decoder entirely.
They suit tasks needing rich understanding but no sequential output.
Every position attends freely to every other position, both before and after it.
The final encoder output, enriched with context, becomes the model's own final product.
A small classification head often gets added on top for task-specific predictions.
BERT stands as the single most influential encoder-only model, covered in the very next topic.
Dropping the decoder reduces total computation, an efficiency benefit for understanding-only tasks.
They suit tasks like Sentiment Analysis and Named Entity Recognition well.
Next up: Decoder-Only Models, the opposite architectural family, dropping the encoder instead.
